question: Does integer translation registration suppress the one retained warm-pixel cue at 22.7 s that PR #7913 visually described as a wall indicator shifting during camera movement?
H: On the exact same ten decoded frames and fixed warm-pixel threshold used by PR #7913, translation-aligning the preceding warm mask will reduce the 22.7 s new-warm-pixel count from the prior value 186 to below 40, without a registration shift at the search boundary.
T: One candidate invocation decodes source-video seconds [21.5,23.5) at 5 fps to 320x280 RGB. For each adjacent pair, search integer dx,dy in [-16,16] minimizing median absolute integer-luma error over y=30..229, excluding the prior weapon mask x=130..189,y=145..229 and center reticle x=156..164,y=96..104. Tie-break by rounded score, Manhattan shift, |dy|,dy,dx. Compare newly appearing warm pixels before and after translating the prior mask. Warm predicate and threshold are fixed from referenced A01: R>=170, 45<=G<=190, B<=95, R>=1.25*G; >=40 pixels triggers.
D: First require the unregistered ten-count vector to equal the retained A01 reference [4,15,96,0,0,0,186,213,176,57], otherwise STOP_CONTROL_DIVERGENCE. HOLD if the 22.7 s registration reaches the +/-16 px search boundary. PASS_LOCAL_TRANSLATION_SUPPRESSION only if the unregistered 22.7 s cue triggers and the registered count is <40; otherwise FAIL_WALL_CUE_NOT_SUPPRESSED. This gate concerns one reference-frame artifact only; the 21.9 s muzzle-flash cue is an expected remaining confound and is not a detector PASS.
C: The apparent wall indicator label comes from the two-frame visual review retained in PR #7913, not an independent semantic label. Camera motion may include rotation/parallax; a moving enemy may resemble background motion; global translation can erase relevant motion or preserve unrelated color changes.
U: One edited historical video, ten frames, one translation-only method, and one manually described reference artifact. No actual enemy classification, detector precision/recall, current-main V39 runtime response, live input, physical release, task effect, survival, recovery, or MAP01 success is measured.
construction_test: python3 -B -m unittest -v test_candidate.py — 3 passed before freeze
runtime: Host macOS Python 3.14.5, NumPy 2.5.2, FFmpeg 8.1.2. OrbStack Docker server responds, but docker image inventory returned an unsupported containerd blob read error; no image pull or container invocation was attempted.
network: Candidate consumes only the retained local video; no network access, game, model, GUI, or OS input.
